title: Internal Land Forming Processes
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Cut out continents from a world map and fit Africa and South America together. Model faulting with foam or layered paper.

skills.key_step: The child names types and causes of earth movements, features made by faulting and their effects on people.

floor.prerequisite: Names the layers of the earth.
floor.question: Which layer do we live on?

steps: Name the force: tension or compression.

board.do: Draw a block of land with two cracks.

board.say: Tension pulls the sides apart. What happens to the middle?

board.do: Write rift valley and two effects.

misconceptions.ask: Which force pulls the crust apart?
misconceptions.repair: Act it with hands: pull apart (tension), push together (compression).

misconceptions.ask: Which feature is made by faulting?
misconceptions.repair: Sort landforms into those made by rivers and those made by faulting.
List faulting effects in Kenya: Rift Valley lakes, hot springs, geothermal power, earthquakes.

misconceptions.ask: How does the Rift Valley help Kenya make electricity?
misconceptions.repair: Show Olkaria on the map with steam pipes.

checks.question: Which force pulls the crust apart?
Give one effect of faulting on people.
checks.answer: any of: earthquakes, hot springs, geothermal power, fertile valley floors, lakes for fishing and tourism

skills.key_step: The child explains continental drift and plate tectonics, gives evidence, and links plate movement to rifts, mountains, earthquakes and volcanoes.

floor.prerequisite: Names the layers of the earth.
floor.question: Which layer lies below the crust?

steps: Say the continents were once one: Pangaea.
Say plates move on the mantle.
Name what happens where plates meet or part.

board.do: Draw Africa and South America apart.

board.say: What do you notice if we push them together?

board.do: Write Pangaea and two pieces of evidence.

misconceptions.ask: Have the continents always been in the same place?
misconceptions.repair: Fit the coasts of Africa and South America together.

misconceptions.ask: How fast do the plates move?
Give one piece of evidence for continental drift.
misconceptions.repair: Show matching fossil maps across the Atlantic.

misconceptions.ask: Does each country have its own plate?
misconceptions.repair: Show the African plate covering many countries.

checks.question: What was Pangaea?
checks.answer: the single land mass the continents once formed

checks.question: What happens where plates pull apart?
